text: 🇲🇽🎓 Sheinbaum doubled the goal: 400,000 new high school places so no teenager is left out. "We will have 400,000 new places, because the best place for teenagers to be is in school. The President doubled the goal — we had planned 200,000 places, and she told us we must make it 400,000." — Tania Rodríguez, Undersecretary of Upper Secondary Education In 2025, 88 schools were built or expanded (44,000 places). In 2026: 485 more schools, 156,240 places, over 10 billion pesos. Enrollment for the new Bachillerato Nacional "Margarita Maza" is open.

But first we are going to ask the teachers: what is your opinion?" — President Claudia Sheinbaum Sheinbaum cited US court rulings that found social media platforms harm children's mental and physical health. After the school-council debate, Mexico will discuss wider regulation of addictive platform design.

text: 🇲🇽⚖️ A US court ruled Meta legally responsible for the harm its platform design causes children — and ordered the design changed. "The problem is not bad users posting negative content; it is a system designed to foster overuse, unwanted contact, and exposure to unwanted, harmful content." — Dr. Ravi Iyer, USC Neely Center, on the New Mexico v. Meta ruling The New Mexico ruling is the first to force a platform to modify design decisions: age verification, hidden like counts for minors, no push notifications at night or school hours, usage time caps, and private-by-default teen accounts — for 5 years.

🇲🇽📱 Meta's own internal research: 13% of Instagram users aged 13-15 received unwanted sexual advances in a single week. "Meta's own internal research revealed that 13% of Instagram users between 13 and 15 years old had received some unwanted sexual advance in the last 7 days." — Dr. Ravi Iyer, former Meta data-science research lead, at Mexico's morning press conference The figure comes from Meta's internal research made public in the New Mexico v. Meta litigation. A related internal survey found 19.2% of children 13-15 saw unwanted nudity or sexual content in one week. Iyer, now at USC's Neely Center, spent 4.5 years at Meta designing social networks.

🇲🇽💻 <u>MEXICO'S TECH ENGINE: COMPUTER EXPORTS UP 178%, DRIVING THE EXPORT BOOM</u>

Mexico's exports of data-processing machines surged 177.57% from January to May — 76.75 of every 100 additional export dollars came from this sector alone, per a Banco BASE analysis of Banxico and Inegi figures reported by El Economista. Servers and processing units shipped to the US hit 60.4 billion dollars in the first half, against 80.5 billion in all of 2025. Total exports reached a record 389.7 billion dollars, up 24.62%, with Chihuahua and Jalisco leading the AI-hardware corridors. The AI revolution runs on hardware assembled in Mexico.

🇲🇽🚁 <u>NAVY HELICOPTER MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING IN JALISCO — NO FATALITIES</u>

A Mexican Navy Mi-17 was forced into "a controlled emergency landing" in Tamazula de Gordiano, Jalisco, while flying surveillance to prevent illicit activity. Three crew members were lightly injured; no lives lost, the Navy confirmed, and the cause is under investigation. While US hawks fantasize about sending their own troops south, Mexico's armed forces are the ones patrolling Mexican soil — every day, in every state.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>THE NARCO-FILTER IS READY — AND NOT ONE PARTY HAS DARED TO USE IT</u>

Mexico's Security Cabinet is fully prepared to vet 2027 candidates for organized-crime ties through the INE's new special commission, Sheinbaum confirmed. The catch: "hasta la fecha todavía no se recibe ninguna solicitud" — not a single party has requested a background check, even though thousands of candidacies may need review. The tool to keep narco money off the ballot exists; the parties simply refuse to touch it. Meanwhile the UIF runs permanent money-laundering investigations — and the 500,000 dollars recovered from the García Luna case just landed in the Treasury.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>300 DAYS IN AN ICE CELL: MEXICAN JOURNALIST HELD AFTER CHARGES DISMISSED</u>

Carlitos Ricardo Parias, a journalist from Puebla, marks 300 days locked in ICE's Adelanto processing center in California — the longest detention of a journalist ever recorded in the United States. He was shot by an agent during his arrest; a judge dismissed every criminal charge for good, yet deportation proceedings grind on. The Intercept documented him living among cockroaches in an unsanitary cell, drinking water with worms in it, his bullet-wounded arm turning purple without medical care. That's how the "land of press freedom" treats a Mexican journalist.
